novelty.justification: The claim's wording, “whether an EHR foundation model's INTERNAL representation encodes the TEMPORAL DIRECTIONALITY (A-before-B vs B-before-A asymmetry) that defines progression,” follows a new mechanism/measurement route: it hypothesizes that directional disease progression is represented internally and is causally load-bearing, rather than merely transferring prediction to a new dataset. The closest prior works I found were Foresight (2024) and Curiosity (2025) on longitudinal EHR event forecasting, the 2025 “Causal Representation Learning for Predicting Autoimmune Disease Progression” framework, and “Tokenization Tradeoffs in Structured EHR Foundation Models” (2026), using searches such as “EHR foundation model temporal directionality internal representations,” “sequence reversal counterfactual disease progression transformer,” “EHR model causal representation probing,” and “A before B versus B before A EHR”; these address forecasting, temporal encoding, or output-level counterfactuals, not the proposed internal forward/reverse asymmetry. The step from that work to this claim requires a new core relationship—directed progression pairs should show reversal-sensitive internal risk representations while comorbidity pairs should not—although it uses established probes and steering rather than introducing a general new interpretability paradigm, supporting a high-but-not-paradigm-level score.
